title: A Day in the Life of a Software Engineer
paragraphs: Nurlan Seitkali works as a software engineer at a tech startup in Almaty. He is Kamila's older brother. This is a typical working day for him.

He starts work at 9 a.m. from home. He makes coffee, opens his laptop, and checks his messages. He has a team meeting at 9:30 — they discuss what everyone is working on and what problems they need to solve.

From 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., he does his main work: writing and testing code. He needs full concentration during this time, so he turns off notifications and puts on headphones. He takes a break at 1 p.m. for lunch.
In the afternoon, he has a call with a client to discuss a new feature request. Then he does a code review — checking the work done by other developers on his team. He makes notes and gives feedback.
At 5 p.m., he writes a short summary of what he achieved today and what he will do tomorrow. He turns off his laptop and does something physical — he goes for a run or does a workout.

Nurlan loves his job, but he also knows that the work-life balance is important. 'I make time for my family, sport, and reading,' he says. 'A good engineer has to look after their mind, not just their code.'

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Nurlan, what does a software engineer actually do all day?

dialogue.speaker: Nurlan
dialogue.text: I write code, do code reviews, attend meetings, and talk to clients.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Do you make a lot of decisions in your job?

dialogue.speaker: Nurlan
dialogue.text: Yes — I make decisions about how to solve technical problems every hour.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: And do you have to work overtime much?

dialogue.speaker: Nurlan
dialogue.text: Sometimes, but I try to have a good work-life balance. It's essential.
